headline: Chitradurga faces child marriage pressure and weak parent-child bonds, risking adolescent health and nutrition outcomes
summary: Chitradurga district confronts multiple challenges affecting child nutrition and development. Child marriage remains a persistent threat, with cases involving physical coercion and familial pressure documented as recently as 2025. Local volunteers report a critical breakdown in parent-child communication, leaving young girls emotionally vulnerable, especially as parents leave children alone while working in fields. The district recorded nearly 2000 teen pregnancies over three years ending 2025, reflecting broader risks to maternal and child health. These social pressures, combined with weak family supervision, undermine conditions for healthy child development and nutrition security.

reasons.detail: Chitradurga recorded nearly 2000 teen pregnancies in three years, reflecting early childbearing risks that compromise maternal nutrition and child health outcomes.
Child marriages continue despite interventions; a 2025 case involved a 13-year-old Class 8 girl resisting forced marriage through physical struggle.
Parents working in fields leave girls alone at home; volunteers report missing parent-child bonds and lack of open communication, increasing vulnerability.
Local volunteers identify social media as a risk factor, with girls seeking affection externally when emotional support at home is lacking.
